text:
marcus: heads up — seeing slow memory growth after long-context runs when kernel selection toggles mid-request. spikes happen right after a batch-switch, looks like some prefetched KV pages get re-used by the next request. attaching small log snippet below.

devin: can you paste the exact logs + a repro? curious if this is the same cross-request contamination we saw last month.

marcus: sure, here's the relevant lines from a canary run (sanitized):
```
[2026-02-12 21:03:12.431] kv_prefetch: req=abcd1234 pid=437 page_idx=7 size=4096 align=16 kernel=opt_short
[2026-02-12 21:03:12.432] page_attach: prev_req=efgh5678 new_req=abcd1234 offset=-1 overlap=1
[2026-02-12 21:03:12.432] kv_page_owner_mismatch: page=0x7f9c tag=efgh5678 attach_req=abcd1234
```
looks like a prefetch happens, kernel switch occurs (we pick the short-seq kernel) and later an attach reuses a page that still has the prev_req tag.

alina: that offset=-1 ring alarm for me — sounds like page index arithmetic after the kernel switch is using a different fragment size, so page boundaries shift. do we have request_id tagging guaranteed before prefetch?

marcus: we do set page->tag = req_id at allocation in the normal path, but the fast prefetch path does a lightweight touch and defers the full attach until later. code has: `if (!page->owned_by_current_req()) attach()` — my hunch is a race where attach assumes it owns the page because prefetch and kernel-switch interleave.

priya: quick mitigation suggestion: make prefetch write the tag atomically (store-release) and add a debug assert on attach that fails loudly if tag != req_id. disabling prefetch reduces memory-growth but adds ~4-8% tail latency in our bench.

devin: agree on the assert. i also want a fingerprint check on the KV block header for debug builds — if checksum mismatches, throw a hard fail instead of silently reusing. cheaper than a full copy and helps catch contamination quickly.

marcus: repro steps i've been using locally: `./tools/runtime_perf --long-context --batch-switch --prefetch=on --seed=42 --repeat=2000` — reproduces within ~30-50 iterations on my devbox. attaching the tiny repro script in thread.

marcus: profiler note: at the boundary we see a hotspot chain `kv_prefetch -> kernel_switch -> page_attach` and a short-lived increase in RSS that never gets reclaimed until eviction; looks like page metadata isn't being cleared on detach in the fast path.

alina: can you open a minimal test in the kv-regression suite that reproduces with `--deterministic-kernel-switch`? we need CI coverage before we hotfix.

devin: i'm going to add two changes: 1) atomically set tag in prefetch path, 2) add a defensive `if (page->tag != req_id) { mark_corrupt(); detach(); }` in debug and run perf bench. will measure perf delta. i'll also add a unit that forces kernel-switches mid-request.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary runtime image with pr/kv-fix prefetched to infra-canary at 03:00 UTC.

priya: note — disabling prefetch in canary config is a cheap toggle if we see any regression; keep us posted.

devin: opened draft PR: https://git.company/repo/pull/4321 (WIP) — includes assert + atomic tag write + repro test. running bench now, will post numbers shortly.

marcus: thanks — assigning this one to @devin + @marcus. putting kv/bug/critical on it. i'll gather a short blam repro and add to postmortem if this made it to prod.
